lesson_title: VAT, UIF, Tariffs and Exchange Rates: the Numbers in Your Wallet
hook_text: The till slip says R276. The shop kept R240. Guess who got the other R36 — and why taking 15% off gives the WRONG answer.
clip_script: R240 microwave. Add fifteen percent VAT — R36 — and the shelf says R276. Easy. Now go backwards: the slip says R276, what was the price before tax? Everyone takes fifteen percent off. Everyone is wrong. Fifteen percent of 276 is 41,40 — too big, because 276 is already the taxed number. The slip is 115 percent of the truth, so DIVIDE by 1,15: R240, exactly. Next, your payslip. UIF: one percent of gross. Slide the comma — R8 400 becomes R84. And here's the secret: your boss pays another R84 you never see. The fund gets R168; your slip shows R84. Now the phone shop. Deal A: R99 a month plus 75 cents a minute. Deal B: no fee, R1,45 a minute. Talk 100 minutes? B wins, R145 to R174. Talk 200? A wins, R249 to R290. They swap at about 141 minutes. Fixed fee for the big talker, pay-as-you-go for the quiet one. Direction and rate — that's the whole wallet.
visual_style: A till slip unrolling with the VAT line glowing; a payslip splitting into two R84 coins, one visible and one sliding in from the employer's side; two phone-deal cost lines racing on a graph and crossing at 141 minutes.
mood: Sharp, consumer-savvy, slightly conspiratorial — the friend who checks the slip before leaving the till.
pacing: Quick on the VAT trap, a beat of surprise on the hidden R84, accelerating through the phone-deal race to the crossing point.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and out-calculate every till, payslip and phone deal.
